description:
## What

The "lazy-init class-level store with @@store + @@store_lock" pattern is duplicated in 3 files:

- `src/fetcher/rate_limiter_registry.cr` (RateLimiterRegistry.store)
- `src/fetcher/circuit_breaker.cr` (CircuitBreaker::Registry.store)
- `src/fetcher/url_validator.cr` (URLValidator.validated_store)

Each follows the same shape:

```crystal
@@store : SomeStore? = nil
@@store_lock = Mutex.new

def self.store : SomeStore
  @@store_lock.synchronize { @@store ||= SomeStore.new }
end
```

## Why

DRY violation. Adding a new registry means copying the pattern. The shape is mechanical and identical.

## How

Extract a module-level helper:

```crystal
module LazyStore(T)
  @@instance : T? = nil
  @@lock = Mutex.new

  def self.instance : T
    @@lock.synchronize { @@instance ||= T.new }
  end

  def self.instance=(value : T)
    @@lock.synchronize { @@instance = value }
  end

  def self.reset!
    @@lock.synchronize { @@instance = nil }
  end
end
```

Or use a macro. Each registry then declares `LazyStore(MyStore).instance` instead of hand-rolling the lazy init.

## Counter-considerations

Crystal modules can't have generics in the same way classes can. May need a macro or a different abstraction. Alternatively, a single `class Registry(T)` generic class could host the lazy-init logic.

## Done when

- All 3 sites use the shared helper
- No more hand-rolled `@@store` / `@@store_lock` pairs
- Full spec suite still green
title: Refactor: deduplicate lazy @@store init pattern (3 places)
